claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit in the UK.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me:
- How many children you have
- Their names (or just first names is fine)
- Their ages

This will help me understand your situation and guide you through the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child. My son Alex is 16 years old, and he lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a 16-year-old son named Alex who lives with you in the UK.

Since Alex is 16, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's continuing in approved education or training. 

**Could you please tell me: Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** 

For example, is he:
- Attending school or college doing A-levels, T-levels, or similar qualifications?
- In approved training or an apprenticeship?
- Or has he left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's actually left education recently. He finished school and has been trying to figure out what to do next, so he signed up with the local careers service to get some advice and help with his options.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know that Alex has left education and registered with a careers service.

According to the rules, when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks.

**To help me assess this properly, could you tell me approximately when Alex left education and when he registered with the careers service?** 

I need to understand if he's still within that 20-week period.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school a few weeks ago, maybe around 2 months back, and he registered with the careers service pretty much right after that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So Alex left school about 2 months ago and registered with the careers service shortly after.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Has Alex started any paid work?** Specifically, is he working 24 hours or more per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started working yet. He's just been focusing on figuring out his next steps with help from the careers service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex isn't working yet.

One more question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?** For example, is he claiming Employment and Support Allowance, Universal Credit, or any other benefits in his own name?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me make sure I have everything correct before making my assessment:

- You have a 16-year-old son named Alex
- He lives with you in the UK
- He left education about 2 months ago
- He registered with a careers service shortly after leaving education
- He is not working 24 hours or more per week
- He is not receiving any benefits in his own right

Just one final question: **Do you yourself live in the UK, and are you the person who would be claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's all correct. I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester - and yes, I would be the one claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

When a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service, Child Benefit can continue for up to **20 weeks**. Since Alex left school about 2 months ago (approximately 8-9 weeks) and registered with the careers service shortly after, you're still well within this 20-week eligibility period.

Additionally:
- Alex isn't working 24 hours or more per week
- He's not claiming benefits in his own right
- He lives with you in the UK
- You're responsible for him

**Important things to note:**
- This eligibility will continue until the 20-week period ends (from when he registered with the careers service)
- If Alex starts an apprenticeship, returns to approved education/training, or finds work within this period, his eligibility may change
- If he starts working 24 hours or more per week, you would no longer be eligible

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you should apply as soon as possible. If you're already receiving it, it should continue during this 20-week period.
